The diagnosis codes for severe bleeding (*Diagnosekoder for alvorlig blødning*) define the clinical criteria used to track the incidence of major bleeding events among patients diagnosed with atrial fibrillation [^src1]. This specific classification system, documented in the 2023 AFDK report, comprises 21 distinct diagnosis codes that focus exclusively on gastrointestinal bleeding and its direct symptomatic presentations [^src1]. Because the data is derived from a single reporting snapshot, no longitudinal trends or temporal shifts in code utilization can be established.

The codes are systematically organized by anatomical location and chronicity. The gastric ulcer categories lead the classification, spanning from acute gastric ulcers with hemorrhage, such as [[dk25-0|DK25.0]], to those complicated by both bleeding and perforation, like [[dk25-2|DK25.2]] [^src1]. Similar structural pairings exist for duodenal ulcers (starting at [[dk26-0|DK26.0]]), gastroduodenal ulcers (starting at [[dk27-0|DK27.0]]), and broader gastrointestinal ulcers (starting at [[dk28-0|DK28.0]]) [^src1]. 

Beyond localized ulcerations, the framework includes inflammatory conditions and generalized bleeding symptoms. Acute hemorrhagic gastritis is captured under [[dk29-0|DK29.0]], while acute hemorrhagic duodenitis is specified as [[dk29-8a|DK29.8A]] [^src1]. The list concludes with three overarching symptomatic codes that serve as critical catch-alls for severe bleeding events where a specific ulcer might not be immediately identified: hematemesis (vomiting blood) under [[dk92-0|DK92.0]], melena (black, tarry stools) under [[dk92-1|DK92.1]], and unspecified gastrointestinal bleeding under [[dk92-2|DK92.2]] [^src1]. Together, these 21 codes form a comprehensive net for identifying severe gastrointestinal hemorrhage in atrial fibrillation quality indicators [^src1].
